title: LLM4DV: Using Large Language Models for Hardware Test Stimuli Generation
problem: Hardware design verification requires manual generation of complex test stimuli to validate functional equivalence against specifications. This test generation process is labor-intensive and specific to each hardware design.
motivation: Automated and efficient hardware test stimuli generation reduces engineering effort and improves design reliability and robustness.
method: LLM4DV automates the creation of test inputs for hardware verification by having multiple large language models (AI systems trained on text) work together using refined prompting techniques—different ways of asking the models to generate tests. Rather than manually creating tests for each chip design, the framework tests six different models and six different prompting strategies across eight hardware designs to discover which combinations work best.
key_novelty: Using coordinated large language models (multiple AI systems working together) with refined prompting to automatically generate hardware test inputs.
contributions: Open-source LLM4DV benchmarking framework for automated hardware test generation
Evaluation of six LLMs with six distinct prompting strategies
Insights for LLM development in hardware verification automation

metrics.other: Framework evaluation and LLM prompting strategy effectiveness

limitations: Limitations and scope constraints are not discussed in the abstract.
